key_insight: Orchestrated large language models can check whether real-world stroke care follows clinical guidelines even when no computer-interpretable guideline exists.
clinical_relevance: This could make guideline adherence auditing more practical for hospitals by using routine text records and written guidelines instead of requiring manual rule coding.
method: Extracted patient care traces from discharge letters using LLM-based components.
Identified normative rules from textual stroke guidelines and translated them into executable scripts.
Computed a Trace Conformance Indicator to measure compliance across the event log.
evidence_signal: In Alessandria Hospital stroke care data, hundreds of patient traces were assessed against 50 guideline-derived rules, and more than 86% of available traces were conformant.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of text extraction and rule translation, so outputs should be validated carefully before operational use.
paper_title: LLM-Orchestrated Conformance Checking in Stroke Care Without Computer-Interpretable Guidelines
